tob-10464: George Fox founded the Religious Society of Friends — the Quakers — after concluding that truth comes from an inner light, not from priests or books. His autobiography recounts his spiritual crisis, his preaching tours across England, and his imprisonments for refusing to conform. It is the founding narrative of a movement that would shape ideas of conscience, equality, and peace.
tob-4264: The Hermetic Triumph — laid to Limojon de Saint-Didier — is a 1689 talk-piece on the wise-stone, mooting gold-lore’s privities with wit and learning. The nameless work charmed 1600s adepts. Its talk-form makes deep teaching lively. A classic of French gold-lore letters.
tob-14364: Jesus Christ’s Wisdom — from the Nag Hammadi hoard — gives the risen Christ’s word on godly wisdom and the world’s making. This Gnostic opening ranks with the hoard’s finest texts. The work lights the rich manyness of early Christendom.
tob-10264: Helena Blavatsky’s Isis Unveiled — 1877 — is the huge founding book of God-wisdom, a key to the riddles of old and new science and faith. Its two fat volumes awed and angered readers. The two books set the fellowship alight. The book stays its great source-book.
cia-0000109064: A November 1967 report on the state of Cuba-Soviet economic relations and Western Europe's unease about them. While Moscow normalized trade with Havana, European allies worried about being dragged into the embargo politics. The document maps a three-cornered tension: Havana, Moscow, and a nervous Western Europe.
cia-0000112364: A May 1986 directive on conducting offensive strategic counterintelligence operations — the truncated title cuts off the target. Going on offense meant turning enemy spies, feeding disinformation, and striking first. The document opens a rare window onto the CIA's playbook for fighting the spy war aggressively.
cia-0000119764: An October 1956 roundup of reactions to the Hungarian revolt. The world watched Budapest with horror and admiration — and did nothing. The document tallies the responses: the condemnations, the sympathy, and the silence that sealed Hungary's fate.
cia-0000124264: A January 1960 report on the Soviet space research program's space vehicles — the hardware of the cosmic contest. Rockets, capsules, and probes were assessed like divisions of an army. The document is the order of battle for a war fought in orbit.
cia-0000126864: A November 1968 report on the current disarray in Zanzibar — the island half of Tanzania, four years after its revolution. President Karume's regime was erratic and isolated, and the island was coming apart. The document captures the CIA watching a tiny revolution eat itself.
cia-0000126964: A January 1967 report on the situation in Panama. The canal zone dispute poisoned everything — nationalism rising against American control. The document captures the slow-burn crisis that would explode in the 1968 coup and Torrijos's rise.
cia-0000132264: Situation Report 571 on European reactions — the truncated title withholds to what. The continent's capitals weighed in as the war approached its climax. The document tallies the allies: who stood firm, who wavered, who wanted out.
cia-0000132564: A 1960 report: Guatemalan leftists encouraged by the Salvadoran coup. One country's upheaval heartened the neighbors' radicals. The document is the encouragement: the leftists, emboldened.
cia-0000134264: Item 8 in a 1960 Latin America series: plans for a Cuban May Day rally — and item 9, Brazilian opinion, the truncated title suggests. The revolution's showcase and the continent's view. The document is the double bill: the rally and the reaction.
cia-0000136264: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN providing views of the situation and requesting authority to continue — the truncated title cuts off what. The assessment and the ask, together. The document is the pitch: the views, given — the authority, sought.
cia-0000136364: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN, from WELLBANK, summarizing the attitude of the Calligeris group — the truncated title cuts off toward what. The mood, assessed. The entry is the summary: the attitude, gauged.
cia-0000136864: A 1954 cable to the senior representative at LINCOLN reporting that no action would be taken on a reference — the truncated title cuts off which. The stand-down. The document is the inaction: the decision, negative.
cia-0000136964: A 1954 cable to the senior representative at LINCOLN requesting approval for press conferences — the truncated title suggests more. The public face, planned. The document is the approval: the conferences, sought.
cia-0000137464: A 1963 Special National Intelligence Estimate, numbered 83.4-63, on security conditions in Costa Rica. The SNIE format meant the full community's judgment. The document is the estimate: the republic's security, weighed.
cia-0000141164: An estimated 1961 list of pilots. The airmen, named. The document is the roster: the pilots, listed.
un-ga-res-a-69-64: Resolution A/69/64, cataloged with the year 2008 — the session number and year mismatch once more. The entry preserves the designation and flags the inconsistency, describing nothing it cannot prove.
un-sc-res-364: Security Council Resolution 364, cataloged with the year 1966 — the numbering suggests 1974, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
un-sc-res-1764: Security Council Resolution 1764, cataloged with the year 1995 — the numbering suggests 2007, a deep mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
cia-0000136564: A 1960 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000136564. The Spanish documents accumulated. The document is the accumulation: the files, many.
cia-0000136764: An estimated 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136764, the archive's date uncertain. The circa set. The entry is the circa: the dating, soft.
un-ga-res-52-164: General Assembly Resolution 52/164, adopted in 1998 — this one aligns. The late-nineties Assembly deciding. The designation and year are certain; the subject belongs to the text.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d64: President Roosevelt to Generalissimo Chiang, October 27, 1943 — Document 64. The president wrote China's leader. The message is the fourth ally: Chiang, addressed.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d164: A memorandum by the British delegation to the Moscow Conference — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 164. The British put their position on paper. The memo is the position: the delegation, recording.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d264: An editorial note — Cairo-Tehran 1943, Document 264. The editors' joint. The note is the joint: the pieces, fitted.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d364: Combined Chiefs of Staff minutes, November 29, 1943 — Document 364. The next day, the planners met again. The minutes are the next: the chiefs, returning.
arxiv-2605-08864: Online estimation updates beliefs as data streams in, and EM-compressible variants do it cheaply. ZhiMing Li and Yue Song add higher-order equilibrium tracking, following not just where the estimate sits but how it curves. The 2026 paper is statistical signal processing for streaming data.
arxiv-2605-09064: Managing wildlife — how many deer to cull, where to protect — means acting on uncertain science. Olivier Gimenez, Abby Keller, and Cyril Milleret apply Bayesian decision theory, carrying uncertainty all the way from inference to action. The 2026 paper is statistics in service of conservation.
arxiv-2605-09264: Treatment effects estimated in one population must be transported to another — with honest sensitivity to what might differ between them. Pengyun Wang builds nested sensitivity envelopes for transported quantile treatment effects. The 2026 paper is causal inference designed to travel well.
arxiv-2605-09564: Full waveform inversion reconstructs the Earth's interior from seismic waves, but cycle skipping — matching the wrong wiggle — ruins it. Xinru Mu, Omar M. Saad, Shaowen Wang, and Tariq Alkhalifah mitigate it with max-pooling-based approximate envelopes. The 2026 paper is geophysics that stays on the right cycle.
arxiv-2605-09664: Malware evolves daily, so analyzers must learn continually — without hoarding old samples forever. Zahra Asadi, Haeseung Jeon, Sohyun Han, and colleagues do it memory-free with FreeMOCA for malicious code analysis. The 2026 paper is cybersecurity that keeps learning without remembering.
arxiv-2605-09764: Evolutionary search needs capable brains guiding it; bigger LLMs help, but better search architectures help even more. Temoor Tanveer shows stronger search architectures can substitute for larger LLMs — LEVI. The 2026 paper argues convincingly for efficiency over brute scale, every time.
arxiv-2605-09964: Protein-protein interactions need good priors; learning the interaction prior in a model-agnostic way improves prediction. Ziqi Gao, Chenyi Zi, Zijing Liu, and colleagues develop the model-agnostic approach. The 2026 paper is computational biology on who binds whom. It predicts binding without model-specific tricks.
plos-pone-0003464: Neurobiologists gave a nerve-wrapping protein a new job in this 2008 paper. Myelin-associated glycoprotein, or MAG, appears in Schwann cells before they start insulating nerves, but what switches it on was unknown. The team showed the RING finger protein 10 regulates MAG's transcription, naming the control that kicks off myelination.
plos-pone-0003564: Toxicologists caught anthrax's edema toxin working in two waves in this 2008 paper. The toxin, an enzyme that floods cells with signaling molecules, modulated the PKA and CREB pathways in distinct early and late phases. Dissecting that two-phase attack reveals how anthrax disrupts host cells with timed precision.
plos-pone-0003664: In 2008, a team found HIV waking immune cells by a side door. The virus switched on macrophages, the long-lived cells where it hides, without using Toll-like receptors, the usual alarm bells. The other route shows HIV has more than one way to stir the cells it lives in.
plos-pone-0003764: Manich, Knapp, and Gibert placed a toxin in its family in this 2008 paper. The delta toxin of Clostridium perfringens, one of its three hemolysins, proved sequence-related to beta toxin, NetB, and staphylococcal pore-formers. The kinship reveals a shared pore-punching design behind diverse bacterial weapons.
plos-pone-0003864: Working in 2008, Doheny, Mottus, and Grigliatti proposed a third way cells hush genes. Beyond known silencing systems, they described a telomeric position effect in eukaryotes, where chromosome ends quiet nearby genes. The new mechanism adds to the toolkit of gene control.
plos-pone-0003964: In 2008, Harris, Wayland, and Lan zoomed into schizophrenia's smallest blood vessels. Laser-captured brain microvasculature revealed molecular changes in the illness. The vessel-level view suggests the brain's plumbing is part of schizophrenia's story.
plos-pone-0004064: In 2008, Walsh, Kim, and Maurizio split a protein's two jobs. TRAF6 switched on the NF-kappa-B and MAPK pathways in response to IL-1 and RANKL. Its self-tagging activity proved unnecessary for the switch. The adaptor's signaling role stands apart from its enzyme role.
plos-pone-0004164: In 2009, Agudelo, Galindo, and Ortiz mapped invisible forces on human immunity. They charted the electrostatic landscape of class II HLA molecules fully. Small peptide changes reshaped the charge terrain a lot. The charge maps guide better vaccine peptide design work.
plos-pone-0004264: In 2009, Shorning, Zabkiewicz, and McCarthy found a tumor gene shaping mouse gut cells. Lkb1 loss skewed goblet and Paneth cell production in the small intestine. The multitasking kinase kept gut balance daily. The finding links Lkb1 to intestinal health closely.
plos-pone-0004364: In 2009, a team found invisible malaria spreaders in Kenya. Submicroscopic gametocytes carried antifolate-resistant Plasmodium in western Kenya widely. The hidden carriers spread drug-proof malaria widely. The finding reshapes malaria transmission control. The work shows treatment failing to stop spread fully.
plos-pone-0358864: Training to teach in rural China brings an identity question: who am I becoming as a teacher? This case study follows rural pre-service teachers through an English pedagogy course and traces how their professional identity takes shape. It shows how coursework, not just classroom time, rebuilds how future teachers see themselves and their work.
plos-pone-0355864: Back pain plagues many postmenopausal women, but who is most at risk? This study measured prevalence and risk factors among women attending rehab facilities, then used machine learning to classify cases. The model points physiotherapists toward the patients who need the most attention.
plos-pone-0358964: Smoking damages more than lungs — it may thin the eye’s blood-rich choroid layer. Using Korea’s national health survey data from 2017–2021, this study linked smoking status to choroidal thickness. The association adds the eye to smoking’s long list of victims and gives eye doctors one more reason to ask about cigarettes.
plos-pone-0358464: Spartina, an invasive marsh grass, chokes coastlines — and spotting it from the air is a data-starved problem. This systematic ablation study tested whether training strategy beats network architecture for detecting Spartina in aerial imagery with tiny geospatial datasets. The answer reshapes how ecologists should train AI on small, precious datasets.
plos-pone-0355964: Tumors put the brakes on immune cells — and two proteins, Galectin-9 and B7-H4, may work as a team. This paper identified Galectin-9 as a B7-H4 binding partner and characterized their sugar-dependent interaction that tunes T cell signaling. The partnership is a new target for releasing the immune brakes in cancer therapy.
plos-pone-0358364: Does turf change how soccer is played? This paper studied playing surface effects on match outcomes and formation usage in Major League Soccer. The patterns show whether grass or artificial turf tilts results — and how coaches adapt their formations to the ground beneath their players’ feet.
plos-pone-0357764: Lung cancer’s chemotherapy resistance is a network problem, not a single-gene one. This paper used Boolean-network simplification and rule fitting to unravel chemotherapy resistance in non-small cell lung cancer. The simplified logic maps reveal the molecular switches that flip tumors from drug-sensitive to drug-proof.
plos-pone-0358264: Cannulating sub-millimeter vessels across a whole body demands an extraordinary experimental setup. This paper described constructing just such a rig for full-body micro cannulations of tiny vessels in anatomical research. The setup enables vascular studies at a scale and fineness previously out of reach.
plos-pone-0356464: Related memories interfere with each other — but the timing flips with age. This study found related memories exhibit interference during learning in adults, yet during later retrieval in children. The developmental flip reveals something fundamental about how memory systems mature from childhood to adulthood.
plos-pone-0356764: Working from home glued millions to their chairs. The COVISTRESS international study identified teleworking as the main risk factor for sedentary behavior across countries. The global data make an undeniable case for deliberate movement when the office is the kitchen table.
plos-pone-0352564: Coal shearer drums vibrate violently underground — and their housings eventually crack. This study analyzed the vibration characteristics of the shearer spiral drum and predicted fatigue life of the cutting unit housing under multi-factor coupling. The predictions help prevent catastrophic failures deep in the mine.
plos-pone-0356264: Total knee replacement hides significant blood loss that standard measures miss. This analysis identified independent risk factors for high hidden blood loss following total knee arthroplasty. The risk factors help surgeons anticipate trouble and manage blood wisely — before the patient pays the price.
plos-pone-0357664: Spotting colorectal lesions early saves lives — and AI is getting good at it. This paper used transformer-based deep learning with a multiscale feature interface for colorectal lesion diagnosis. The AI catches subtle lesions that tired human eyes miss, potentially shifting diagnoses earlier.
plos-pone-0328664: Across a competitive volleyball microcycle, jump metrics and perceived recovery tell the training story. This study monitored CMJ-derived jump metrics and subjective recovery in semi-professional women’s volleyball. The combined data help coaches tune training load to keep athletes peaking, not breaking.
plos-pone-0357464: Yoga may sharpen aging minds — and the retina shows it happening. This paper linked retinal neurovascular and mitochondrial function signatures to cognition improvement following yoga exercise in older adults. The eye’s measurable changes mirror the brain’s gains, offering a window into healthy aging.
plos-pone-0357264: Self-driving cars live or die by precise path tracking. This paper developed composite learning-based finite-time nonsingular terminal sliding mode control for intelligent vehicle path tracking. The advanced controller keeps autonomous vehicles glued to their intended paths, even under disturbances.
plos-pone-0357364: Veterinary clinics are businesses too — and their economics shape the care pets receive. This Turkish study used cluster-based classification to map the socio-economic and financial characteristics of companion animal clinics in Ankara Province. The clusters reveal the market’s real structure.
plos-pone-0356364: Premature babies given too much oxygen can develop bronchopulmonary dysplasia and pulmonary hypertension. This paper investigated the role of connexin 43 — a cell-to-cell communication protein — in that hyperoxia-induced damage. The findings nominate a molecular target for protecting fragile newborn lungs.
plos-pone-0354364: High-purity quartz — essential for semiconductors and solar panels — hides in rare pegmatite deposits. This paper reported the discovery and significance of pegmatite-type high-purity quartz deposits in Shangnan, in China’s North Qinling mountains. The find could ease supply constraints on one of technology’s most critical raw materials.
plos-pone-0351164: Tuberculosis doesn’t just sicken Guatemalans — it bankrupts them. This first national TB costs survey from 2023 measured the burden of catastrophic costs and income inequalities. The findings confront policymakers with the economic violence of TB — and the financial protection patients desperately need.
plos-pone-0354964: Obesity clusters where health, environmental, and socioeconomic disadvantages collide. This paper proposed an ecosyndemic framework for understanding obesity through spatial clustering of disadvantage in the Netherlands. The framework reframes obesity as a geographic injustice — not a personal failure — with clear policy implications.
plos-pone-0346464: Iron supplements change the battlefield between insects and their bacterial invaders. This paper studied how dietary iron supplementation affects bacterial infections in the hemolymph — insect blood — of Manduca sexta caterpillars. The findings reveal iron’s double-edged role in immunity — with implications from pest control to human nutrition.
plos-pone-0353764: Korea’s government subsidizes flu shots — but do the subsidies reach the poor? This population-based study examined socioeconomic differences in influenza vaccination coverage by financial support status. The findings test whether public money genuinely closes the immunization gap or merely subsidizes the already-vaccinated.
plos-pone-0346164: Biological sequences need checksums that handle circular, linear, single- and double-stranded forms. SEGUID v2 extends the classic SEGUID checksums to all of them. The extended standard gives bioinformaticians reliable identifiers for the full menagerie of molecular sequences.
plos-pone-0355464: Cadmium poisons the liver — but a tropical tree extract might defend it. This paper showed Guazuma ulmifolia butanol extract protects against cadmium-induced hepatotoxicity via HO-1/Sirt-1 activation, miRNA–lncRNA modulation, and metabolic reprogramming. The multi-pathway protection lends scientific weight to traditional medicine.
plos-pone-0354664: Centella asiatica — gotu kola — may harbor NRF2 activators with therapeutic promise. The CERES approach — cluster-enabled regression of extract signatures — discovered them using ion-mobility mass spectrometry and k-medoids clustering. The sophisticated discovery pipeline modernizes natural product drug hunting.
europmc-pmc2827364: Drugs that block histone deacetylases can reprogram cancer cells, and this 2010 review surveys the new ones in clinical trials. The authors cover the novel HDAC inhibitors being tested as anti-cancer agents. Their overview maps a promising drug class mid-development. The review captured a moment when epigenetic therapy was moving from lab to clinic.
europmc-pmc2846864: Is grass-fed beef really healthier? This 2010 review compares fatty acid profiles and antioxidant content in grass-fed versus grain-fed beef. The authors gather the nutritional evidence side by side. Their synthesis gives consumers and dietitians data instead of marketing claims about the two production methods.
europmc-pmc2874364: A single resistance gene circled the globe in a hospital superbug. This 2010 paper maps the worldwide spread of the blaOXA-23 gene, which defeats carbapenem antibiotics, in Acinetobacter baumannii. The authors trace its march across continents. Their surveillance warned that last-resort drugs were running out.
europmc-pmc2898064: Genes act in networks, and cancer scrambles them. This 2010 paper builds a human functional protein interaction network and applies it to cancer data analysis. The authors' web finds cancer's weak spots. Their network approach became a template for data-driven oncology.
europmc-pmc6507064: Triple-negative breast cancer is the hardest form to treat because it ignores the hormone drugs that work on other types. A major 2019 trial showed that adding immunotherapy - drugs that rally the patient's own immune system - to chemotherapy changed the outlook. This review explains how that result launched an immunotherapy era for the disease and what treatments are being tested next.
europmc-pmc6514564: Oxidative stress happens when harmful oxidant molecules outnumber the body's antioxidant defenses, upsetting the cell's chemical balance. This review argues the imbalance plays a central role in brain diseases like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's. It walks through how excess oxidants damage neurons, why aging tips the scales, and which antioxidant strategies researchers are testing to slow the decline.
europmc-pmc6548764: Who pays for health - governments, donors, or patients themselves? This Global Burden of Disease analysis tracks health spending across countries: past trends, present patterns, and future projections for aid, public budgets, and out-of-pocket costs. The numbers show where money flows, where it falls short, and what it will take to fund health goals worldwide.
europmc-pmc6693264: When illness strikes, families provide most of the care - often at cost to their own health. This scoping review works toward a universal model of family-centered care: what it should include and how systems can support caregivers. The goal is care that heals the patient without breaking the family.
europmc-pmc6744664: Proteins that look nothing alike can still be kin - if you know how to compare their profiles. HH-suite3 hunts distant relatives through profile hidden Markov models, annotating protein function deeply and fast. The new version speeds the homology searches that fill biologists' days.
europmc-pmc6767464: Mendelian randomization borrows genes as natural experiments - but sneaky pleiotropy can corrupt the results. This guide implements MR-PRESSO and GCTA-GSMR, two methods that sniff out pleiotropic variants in large genetic studies. The toolkit helps researchers trust their causal claims.
gao-gaoreports-b-309964: A Government Accountability Office bid-protest ruling dated November 9, 2007, covering two filings by ITT Industries Space Systems, LLC. The defense contractor challenged an award in the space-systems arena, and the decision applies federal procurement law to the disputed competition. The case shows GAO refereeing high-stakes defense contracting, where a single award can be worth hundreds of millions of dollars.
gao-gaoreports-b-299864: Harris Corporation triple-filed its 2007 contract protest, and GAO's combined ruling answers all three. The tech-and-defense firm said the award was flawed; the call works each claim to a close. Big-ticket bid wars like this are where protest law gets its real-world workout.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-764: Federal timber sales were leaving money on the stump in 2007 — GAO's report says the Forest Service could run its field-level sales tighter. The findings target the ground-level economics of public logging. The report's pitch: manage the woods like a business, protect them like a trust.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-564: Homeland Security's tech blueprint kept morphing in 2007 — GAO's report says the enterprise architecture evolved but still wanted fixes. The findings track the moving target in full detail. The report's plea stands: draw the map before building the roads, not after.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-364: The IRS's computers were still full of holes in 2007 — GAO's report says the tax agency had to face its major security weaknesses. The findings demand deeper fixes, not quick patches. The report's warning: the vault of the nation's money cannot have open windows.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-264: The State Department's air fleet got better management in 2007, and GAO's report says a more systematic approach was taking hold. The findings credit the progress. The report shows the diplomats' wings were getting proper oversight. The fleet was finally being flown right.
openalex-w7207874964: Puericultura, the Brazilian practice of scheduled well-child visits, is meant to track how children grow and develop. This study reviews the literature on what these checkups contribute to monitoring child development in primary care, searching SciELO, PubMed, and CAPES journals. The authors synthesize evidence on whether routine monitoring catches problems earlier. A quiet but important question: does showing up for scheduled visits actually change children's health outcomes.
openalex-w7204180964: A slipped disc in the lower back can mean agony, numbness, or weakness down the leg. This English-language paper reviews which adult patients with lumbar disc herniation need surgery and how they fare afterward. The authors weigh the factors behind the surgeon's call. A clinical guide to one of the most common, and most dreaded, back problems.
openalex-w7204259164: Good PE teaching shapes bodies, minds, and social lives at once. This study looks at how physical-education teachers in schools actually teach: their methods and the know-how behind them. The authors reflect on practice in today's classrooms. A grounded study of the subject too often treated as recess.
openalex-w7128505464: For early lung cancer, removing less lung may be enough. This paper reviews the surgical debate over sublobar resection versus full lobectomy for stage IA non-small cell lung cancer. The authors weighed survival and recurrence evidence since the 1995 trial. A thoracic-surgery review of less versus more.
openalex-w4406941864: Insulin resistance may shrink the brain's memory networks. This study linked metabolic dysfunction to gray matter loss in the default-mode and limbic networks of older adults. The authors also flagged hypothalamic changes. A neuroimaging study of metabolism shaping the mind.
pmc-13434664: This 2026 qualitative study asked mental health consumers — patients — about collaboration with clinicians in inpatient care. Their perspectives reveal what genuine partnership looks like from the bed side. The findings push services toward care designed with, not just for, the people receiving it.
pmc-13430064: This 2026 qualitative study examined how nurses maintained boundaries and infection control when returning home from shifts during the pre-vaccination phase of COVID-19. The rituals of decontamination and separation protected families but carried emotional cost. The paper documents a hidden burden of the pandemic's early months.
pmc-13420764: A 2026 qualitative study on what shapes genetic counselors' professional identity. As genetics moves into mainstream medicine, the counselor's role is evolving fast. The study maps the forces — training, scope, recognition — that define who they are professionally.
pmc-13427764: In this 2026 evolutionary genomics paper, the authors used evolutionary stasis — genome regions that barely change — to map multilayered constraints on how viral and mammalian genomes evolve. Invariable sites mark what evolution cannot touch. The approach turns conservation into a discovery tool.
pmc-13455064: A 2026 physical chemistry paper on infrared spectroscopy of protonated water clusters, using the quantum thermal bath method with highly accurate machine-learned potentials. Water's strangest behaviors start at the molecular level. The combination of quantum simulation and machine learning pushes the accuracy of these fundamental measurements.
pmc-13291764: A 2026 international inception cohort study (PATIENCE) on the use of prokinetic agents — drugs that stimulate gut motility — in adult ICU patients. Gut failure in critical illness is common and dangerous. The cohort data show how these drugs are actually used worldwide.
pmc-13424664: A 2026 phase 2b randomized placebo-controlled trial (ELEVATE-IPF) of deupirfenidone versus pirfenidone and placebo in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. The deuterated version may work better with fewer side effects. The trial is the head-to-head test.
pmc-13462264: This 2026 agricultural paper developed the sterile insect technique for the Asian citrus psyllid — the pest spreading citrus greening — determining how many sterile insects are needed. Sterile releases could suppress the pest without pesticides. The numbers are the operational key.
pmc-13423164: In this 2026 cancer paper, myosin VI drove breast cancer progression via SP1/CA9-mediated acidic tumor microenvironment remodeling and M2 macrophage polarization. The motor protein reshaped the tumor's surroundings. The mechanism is a target.
pmc-13562264: A 2026 cross-sectional study of clinical and psychometric predictors of positive alcohol use disorder screens after gastric bypass. Bariatric surgery changes alcohol risk. The predictors guide screening.
pmc-13633364: A 2026 nuclear medicine paper on the prognostic value of volume-based metabolic PET/CT parameters in anaplastic thyroid carcinoma. The aggressive cancer needs better prognostication. The metabolic volumes predicted outcomes.
pmc-13617664: This 2026 review covered quantitative imaging analysis in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy — from phenotypic differentiation to prognostic stratification. Advanced imaging sorts the thick-heart disease's subtypes. The review organizes the prognostic evidence.
pmc-13527164: In this 2026 molecular biology paper, a fluorescent reporter assay revealed ribonucleotides promote mismatch correction in vivo. The RNA building blocks aided DNA repair. The in vivo evidence is the finding.
pmc-13494664: In this 2026 cardiology paper, 24-hour blood pressure variability combined with circadian patterns predicted cardiovascular events in hypertensive patients. The rhythm-aware prediction improved risk stratification. The combination is the advance.
pmc-13576564: A 2026 systematic review on intraoperative ergonomic microbreaks' impact on surgeons' well-being and performance. The tiny breaks helped surgeons. The review is the evidence.
pmc-13407064: This 2026 paper built a machine learning-based risk stratification model to guide cardiopulmonary exercise training in cardiovascular patients. The AI triaged the exercisers. The model is the clinical tool.
pmc-13585464: In this 2026 paper, a machine-learning model (DRC-AHF) accurately predicted diuresis in acute heart failure. The AI forecasted urine output. The model guides diuretic therapy.
pmc-13525164: In this 2026 Philippine study, time to keratometric stability after pterygium excision surgery was measured in a tertiary hospital. The cornea's settling time was quantified. The time guides follow-up.
pmc-13473964: This 2026 paper described development and pilot testing of a shared decision-making encounter aid for weight management decisions. The decision aid was piloted. The development is the implementation science.
pmc-13427064: This 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis examined large language model-based AI tools' impact on physician-patient communication. The AI's communication effects were pooled. The review is the evidence.
pmc-13426464: In this 2026 study, the influence of academic year on dental students' knowledge about syphilis and its oral manifestations was examined. The students' STI knowledge grew with training. The influence is the education finding.
pmc-13428164: A 2026 paper screening key host targets and mechanistically assessing berberine's modulation of host responses to respiratory syncytial virus. The herbal compound's antiviral mechanism was mapped. The screening is the drug discovery.
pmc-13461564: This 2026 multimethod comparative effectiveness analysis examined nucleic acid testing-optimized HIV diagnostic algorithms in clinical practice. The optimized algorithms were compared. The analysis guides HIV diagnostics.
pmc-13421264: A 2026 comparative efficacy study of two photobiomodulation protocols — transcutaneous versus intraoral — in preventing oral mucositis in head and neck cancer (the title is truncated). The light therapies were head-to-head. The comparing guides oncology.
arxiv-2606-16264: AI chat hosts must answer fast for hordes while splitting costly gear. Tropical lifts on-time scores when the job is split — thinker bits here, talker bits there — by smart line-shifts that mind each due time. It is for crews who run big AI front desks.
arxiv-2606-16564: Bots often get can't-do orders — a spot past their reach — and stiff code just stalls. Stretch Odyn bends the math to find the near-best doable move, not the dream move. For bot crews who work against hard walls.
arxiv-2606-16664: A pure math paper on hum-frames. It grows turn-gangs into grander, kinder frames — out to the rim-take, which nets far-off acts. The fine weeds suit turn-frame and hum-frame sages. High, dry, and dense. Rim-takes tame the far edge. Tame rims, clean proofs.
arxiv-2606-16764: Quantum batteries store energy in quantum states — but charging them fast is tricky. This paper shows 'chiral squeezing' (a lopsided quantum squeezing) can charge them: handedness helps. It is a quantum thermodynamics paper for researchers in quantum energy. Handed squeezes beat plain ones.
